scope: Proposition E.1 (Scalar transfer) of the manuscript “Quasipolynomial Bounds for Arithmetic Progressions” (preprints/Quasipolynomial-Bounds-for-Arithmetic-Progressions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 159 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 481eaf7730dc4d58), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 123. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix the degree, an integer ℓ ≥ 2, and ε > 0. There are constants C, C′ > 0 with the following property; C′ depends only on ℓ, and one may take C′ = ℓ + 1. Let p ≥ 2, let I be an integer box of dimension n ≤ p and side lengths Hi, and let g : I → [0, 1] be a niltest of complexity at most p. Let 0 ≤ f ≤ 1 and e−p ≤ λ ≤ 2. Suppose, for every parameter slice B ⊆ I of log cost at most P = (2 + p)C, that EBfg ≤ λEBg + e−P . (E.1) Extend fg and g by zero. Choose integer x, V uniformly from product boxes at scales Hi and Hi/L, respectively, with V having ℓ columns. Sample t uniformly from an integer box in [−epL, epL]ℓ, possibly restricted to one residue in each coordinate modulo a common D ≤ ep, with every restricted side at least Le−2p. If L ≥ B(p) and mini Hi ≥ B(p)LC′ , then Pr x,V   Et fg − (1 + ε)λg  (x + V t) > e−p ≤ e−p . (E.2) The same conclusion holds when the outer law of (x, V ) is dominated by these product laws by ep, and for scale changes by eO(p), after polynomial changes of the log budgets. All complexity and precision requirements are prescribed before choosing L. The conditional law of t remains the stated uniform law on the prescribed parameter slice; arbitrary reweighting of t after observing (x, V ) is not included.
